Body: The toast message uses non-null assertions on `jobs().find(...)`. If the job list refreshes between click and response (or the job finishes), `find` can return undefined and this will throw inside the success path.

This polling interval is created inside a `createResource` fetcher, so it won’t be cleaned up when the dialog component unmounts. Closing/reopening the dialog can accumulate timers and duplicate polling. Switching to `createEffect` + `onCleanup` (and importing them from `solid-js`) ensures proper teardown.

This issue also appears on line 128 of the same file.

This test command is Windows-specific (`ping -n` is not a count flag on most Unix ping implementations), which will make the test hang or fail on non-Windows runners. Use a platform-appropriate ping invocation.

This issue also appears on line 1270 of the same file.

Failure exit codes are only surfaced in the *truncated* output path (cut && file). When a command fails with small/no output (e.g. `exit 3`), `output` is just "(no output)" with no indication that the command failed, which contradicts the PR description (“labels the failure with its exit code”) and makes failures ambiguous in the textual tool output.

Consider always prefixing failed command output with the exit-code status line, and keep the truncation header/file hint only when truncation occurs.

This test currently asserts that a failing command with no output returns exactly "(no output)". If the tool is meant to “label the failure with its exit code” (per PR description), this expectation should be updated to include the exit-code status line even when the output isn’t truncated.
The test fixtures use tool id "shell", but the actual shell tool id is "bash" (ShellID.ToolID). This makes the suite pass while the feature is broken in production.

LoopDetection.apply returns the (possibly modified) messages array, but the call site ignores the return value. Assigning it back to msgs makes the mutation/contract explicit and prevents future breakage if apply becomes non-mutating.

Loop detection checks for tool id "shell", but shell tool calls are recorded with ShellID.ToolID ("bash"). As a result, this detector will never count real shell failures and the hint won’t be injected.

The unchanged-file stub returns early without running Instruction.resolve or appending any <system-reminder>. That changes behavior: newly introduced nearby instruction files (e.g. a new AGENTS.md) won’t be attached on subsequent reads if the target file itself is unchanged, because the read is deduped before instruction discovery runs.

findPriorRead normalizes the prior offset with `?? 1`, but the tool execution normalizes `params.offset` with `|| 1` (and the schema currently allows 0 via NonNegativeInt). If a prior call used offset: 0, the read effectively starts at 1, but dedup will never match because `input.offset ?? 1` yields 0 while the current normalized offset is 1.

`formatTime()` only guards against `NaN`, but SDK types can supply `"Infinity"/"-Infinity"` too; this currently renders things like `-Infinitys`. Guard with `Number.isFinite()` before computing elapsed.

This file uses `createResource()` to set up polling intervals, but the returned cleanup function is not used by Solid resources, so the interval will leak (especially when the dialog mounts/unmounts). Use `createEffect()` + `onCleanup()` for the polling lifecycle instead.

The toast message uses non-null assertions on `jobs().find(...)`. If the job list refreshed between the cancel response and this toast, `find` can return `undefined` and crash the UI. Fall back to the jobID when the label can't be resolved.

`/experimental/jobs` is polled by the TUI; including full `output`/`error` for every job can make this response arbitrarily large and cause repeated transfer of large logs every 5s. Consider omitting `output`/`error` from the list response (or truncating / gating behind an explicit query flag) and serving full output via a separate endpoint when needed.

`ping -n 18` is Windows-specific (on Linux/macOS `-n` means “numeric output” and the count flag is `-c`). This will make the test fail on non-Windows runners. Make the ping invocation platform-specific.

`jobCancel` currently returns `true` for any existing job (even if it already finished), because `BackgroundJob.cancel()` returns the current snapshot when status != "running". This makes the client think it successfully cancelled a completed job. Return `true` only when the job transitions to (or already is) `cancelled`.

`formatSessionTranscript` renders file parts as a Markdown link to `item.url`. For generated images this is a `data:` URL, which will inline the entire base64 payload into the transcript, potentially producing multi‑MB output and causing slow renders / copy-paste issues.

Consider omitting the URL when it is a `data:` URL (or replacing it with a short placeholder) and only link when the URL is a normal http(s)/file URL.

Addressed in b6dfca817d. Transcript export now renders inline/unknown file URLs as a short `Generated file: <name>` label, while preserving Markdown links only for `http://`, `https://`, and `file://` URLs. TUI and repository-wide typechecks pass.

`debounceWrites` returns `{ ...storage, ... }`, which materializes getter-based properties (e.g. `length`) into a one-time snapshot. On desktop `AsyncStorage` provides `get length()` (see `packages/desktop/src/renderer/index.tsx:150-152`), so spreading will turn it into a static Promise/number and can break callers that expect `length` to reflect current state.

This test uses `setTimeout` with real time delays, which can be flaky on slower CI runners. This file already uses Bun's `vi` fake timers in other tests (e.g. `src/context/layout-scroll.test.ts`). Consider importing `vi` so the debounce tests can run deterministically.

This issue also appears on line 213 of the same file.

removePersisted now returns a Promise that can reject (e.g., IndexedDB transaction failures), but several call sites invoke it without awaiting/handling (some even omit `void`). This can surface as an unhandled promise rejection at runtime. Consider making removePersisted best-effort by swallowing persistence removal errors (legacy localStorage cleanup already is best-effort), or otherwise ensuring the Promise is always handled.

If a checkpoint commit fails, the controller keeps the state dirty (generation > committed) but never reschedules another attempt. If no further mutations happen, the latest value may never be persisted unless someone explicitly calls drain(). Either clear the dirty state on failure (treat as terminal) or reschedule another attempt after the interval so persistence can recover from transient errors.

`draft-blob-get` converts the stored blob bytes via `Uint8Array.from(data)`, which copies the entire buffer byte-by-byte. For large image blobs this adds avoidable CPU/memory overhead; you can slice the existing underlying ArrayBuffer instead.

`urls` caches `URL.createObjectURL(...)` results and never revokes them. Over time (especially with lots of pasted/previewed images), this can leak memory because the object URLs and underlying blobs stay alive for the lifetime of the app.

`blobReference` creates an object URL for every added image, but there’s no corresponding `URL.revokeObjectURL` when an attachment is removed or the prompt is replaced. This can retain blobs in memory indefinitely during a long-running session.

To prevent legacy blob migration from reintroducing drafts that were deleted while migration was in-flight, the async storage wrapper needs to track removals (not just the last set value). Add a boolean marker that can be checked after migration completes.

`pendingProjection` always returns a single block with mode "live". For non-streaming markdown the real projection (see markdown-stream.ts:52-54) uses mode "full", and the render cache / initialResult logic keys off `${cacheKey}:0:full`. Using "live" here prevents warmed cache entries (from home-session preloading) from being used for the initial render, causing a fallback render + reflow even when HTML is already cached.

`preloadMarkdown` behavior is important for perceived startup/navigation performance (home-session preloading) but the prior unit test for this was removed and there is no replacement coverage for the new worker-based parsing path. Consider reintroducing a test that asserts a preloaded entry is reused by `Markdown` (or, if worker usage makes that hard in bun tests, refactor `preloadMarkdown` to allow injecting a parser/transport for tests).
can you remove tests, no need, just do the one line fix

> can you remove tests, no need, just do the one line fix

Done. Removed the test file, keeping only the one-line fix.

`aria-label` is set to the tooltip text (`tip`), which overrides the button’s visible label/value for assistive tech. This makes the control name verbose and can hide the current state (e.g. LTR/RTL or ON/OFF) from screen readers.

The log field `idleMinutes` currently records the computed idle duration (`idle`), but it’s ambiguous because `idleMinutes` is also the configured threshold variable in this scope. This makes logs harder to interpret/aggregate (actual vs threshold). Consider logging both or structuring the field so it’s self-describing.

The new idle-resume auto-compaction path is behaviorally significant (it can enqueue a compaction task before processing the resumed prompt) but there are no tests covering it yet. Add prompt-level tests to assert: (1) idle >= threshold triggers exactly one compaction.create on step 1 when message count is high, (2) idle < threshold does not, and (3) idle_minutes=0 disables the behavior.

This module installs a `document.addEventListener` handler at module-evaluation time. If this file is ever imported in a non-DOM environment (SSR, Node tooling, some tests), it will throw immediately on import. Guard the registration behind a `typeof document === "object"` check so the module can be safely imported even when `document` is unavailable.

`resolveWhenInputIdle` reads `document.activeElement` unconditionally. Even with the guarded listener above, this function can still be invoked in environments without `document` (e.g. if `decodeVcsDiff` is called from a non-window context), which would throw. Add a fast-path that resolves immediately when `document` is not available.

This test currently only asserts the key exists and is a string; an empty/whitespace-only translation would still pass. Since the intent is to ensure the navigation hint copy is actually present, also assert the value is non-empty after trimming so CI catches missing copy.

`env(titlebar-area-*)` isn’t a valid CSS expression; it reads like a wildcard but CSS `env()` requires a specific variable name. To avoid misleading implementation, list the actual `titlebar-area-*` env vars Electron exposes (x/y/width/height) or describe them without using a non-existent `*` form.

`waitForConnection` disposes the JSHandle only after `jsonValue()` resolves; if `jsonValue()` throws (e.g. navigation/target closed), the handle will leak. Wrapping `jsonValue()` in a `try/finally` ensures disposal on all paths.
Fixed in ef2d99749c. The handle is now disposed in a finally block, including when jsonValue() throws. E2E typecheck and all 8 transport tests pass.

The optional chaining on `children[0]?.id` weakens the assertion: if the child entry were unexpectedly missing, the expectation would still look for `id="undefined"` rather than failing immediately. Since you already assert the array length, use a non-null assertion (or assert the element is defined) to make the test strict.

This issue also appears on line 646 of the same file.

`Message`, `Part`, and `UserMessage` are only used as types in this file (casts and type annotations). Importing them as a value import adds an unnecessary runtime dependency and may break builds when using type-only import enforcement (and the rest of the app typically uses `import type` for SDK types).

`useServer` is imported here but never used in the component, which will trip `noUnusedLocals`/lint rules.

This issue also appears on line 22 of the same file.

`isDefaultServer` treats the local server as "default" when `controller.defaultKey()` is null, but other parts of the UI (e.g. `ServerRowMenu` uses `controller.defaultKey() === key`) only consider explicit defaults. This can make the "Default" tag and the menu state disagree for the local server.
The server dropdown only updates local state (`selectedServer`) and doesn’t affect which server’s models are displayed. This makes the control effectively non-functional.
The server dropdown updates `selectedServer`, but the projects list comes from `layout.projects.list()` (current active server), so selecting a different server doesn’t change what’s shown.

The server dropdown updates `selectedServer`, but the rest of the page still reads data from the currently active server. As a result, changing the selection doesn’t actually switch which server’s providers are shown.
The server dropdown currently only updates `selectedServer` and doesn’t affect the MCP/plugin/skill data sources, so changing the selection has no effect.

`density` is tracked in local component state, but it isn’t persisted and (as far as this PR shows) it isn’t applied anywhere outside this select. That means changing "Interface density" won’t actually affect the UI after leaving the page or reloading.

`unreadBadge` and `focusMode` are stored only in local component state and aren’t connected to `useSettings()` or any platform-level behavior. The controls will reset on navigation/reload and won’t actually affect notifications/badging.

**Blocking — concurrent continuations can silently lose a prompt.** The running check and `job.start()` are separate operations. Two parallel calls can both pass this check. `Job.start()` then starts the first effect but returns that running job to the second call, so the second prompt does not run although both calls can report the first result. Please make ownership atomic: put `context.id` in the new job metadata, verify the returned metadata after `job.start()`, and return the existing running-session error when another call owns the job. This also lets you remove this pre-check and the new `job.get` runtime surface. Add a concurrent regression test. Rough patch: +34 / -6 lines, net +28.

**Blocking bloat; low practical impact.** This rejection appears unnecessary. The normal path already loads and validates the existing child, admits its prompt, starts a new job, backgrounds it, and installs completion notification. Please delete this special rejection and its rejection-only test, unless there is a lifecycle constraint outside this code. If such a constraint exists, state it in the tool description. Rough deletion: +0 / -28 lines, net -28.

**Blocking bloat; negligible practical impact.** A continued session does not use this value; it keeps the model stored on the existing child. Please remove the local variable and put `agent.model ?? parent.model` directly in the `session.create()` input. Rough patch: +1 / -2 lines, net -1.

**Blocking bloat; negligible practical impact.** The exact `settled.content` assertion below already checks `childText` and the full completion envelope. Please remove this duplicate `content` property from `toMatchObject`. Rough patch: +0 / -1 line, net -1.

**Advisory — this test does not execute the child a second time.** The fake execution service at lines 47–50 returns immediately after a session ID enters `completed`. The test therefore admits the second prompt but returns the first run’s old assistant response. Please use a per-session run count, publish different text for each run, and assert that this continuation returns the second response. Rough patch: +8 / -3 lines, net +5.

`buildCliToResources` sets `OPENCODE_VERSION` to a unique `0.0.0-local-${Date.now()}` value. Because the desktop app stages executables under `app.getPath("userData")/cli/<version>/...` (see `installCli` in `background-cli.ts`), each dev run will create a new staged directory and never reuse/clean it, which can lead to unbounded growth in the user's `userData/cli` folder over time.

Consider either (a) adding cleanup/retention logic for older `0.0.0-local-*` staged directories, or (b) using a stable version identifier (e.g. git SHA) and changing staging to re-copy when the source binary changes.

This seemed like a good place to add a warning regarding the new flag since people will probably go to this page to check how to set up their skills.

Previously `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS` was only mentioned in the migration guide, but that meant it was easy to miss.

Let me know if you think this shouldn't be here and I should instead add a section in the migration guide for the new flag.
This step no longer runs on the `beta` ref, so the conditional `${{ (github.ref_name == 'beta' && '--sourcemaps') || '' }}` is now dead code (and can be confusing when reading the workflow).

The bootstrap uses `curl -sL` and then executes the downloaded file; if the request fails (e.g., 404/500) it may still write an error page to `t.sh` and run it. Prefer `-f` to fail on HTTP errors (and keep `-sSL`), matching the safer pattern used elsewhere in these docs.

The header comment says this requires #33010 platform mapping, but the script installs the linux-arm64 binary package directly and writes its own `opencode` shim, so it should work independently. Also, for consistency with other repo scripts (e.g. `./install`), consider using `set -euo pipefail` and a small guard to ensure the script is running inside Termux before writing to `$PREFIX/bin`.

This comment explains skipping `opencode-ai`'s postinstall because of missing android→linux mapping, but the script already forces `--ignore-scripts` and installs the binary package directly. To avoid the comment becoming outdated (e.g., once android mapping is published), consider rephrasing it to focus on the deliberate `--ignore-scripts`/shim approach rather than the current state of published mappings.

The Windows-specific note about Bun support now appears after the new Android (Termux) section, which makes it read as if it applies to Android. Please keep the Windows section contiguous by moving the Bun note back into the Windows subsection (e.g., immediately after the Docker bullet) and placing the Android subsection after it.

`renderer.define` sets `import.meta.env.OPENCODE_VERSION` to `JSON.stringify(process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION)`. When `process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION` is unset, `JSON.stringify(undefined)` yields `undefined`, which can break Vite/esbuild `define` (expects a string expression). Also, the renderer code references `import.meta.env.OPENCODE_CHANNEL`, but the renderer build only defines `VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL`, so `OPENCODE_CHANNEL` will be undefined at runtime unless another plugin defines it.

`model.loading` is derived from `!providersQuery.isSuccess` / `!globalProvidersQuery.isSuccess`, which is also true when the query has errored (not just when it's waiting for the initial handshake). That causes the model selector to disappear indefinitely on provider query failures. Prefer `isPending` (or another "not-yet-settled" signal) so handshake-gated queries still block, but error states don’t get treated as loading forever.

`createLocationSync` updates the `[scope, directory, "path"]` query cache, but `info` is currently wired to `api.location.get(...)` (raw `LocationGetOutput`). That overwrites the cached `Path` shape produced by `loadPathQuery` (state/config/worktree/directory/home) after reconnect/handshake, and will break any consumers expecting `Path`. Map the response to `Path` (same as `loadPathQuery`) before storing it in the query cache.

`root.querySelector('[data-markdown-key="initial"]')` gates `firstPaint` on *any* initial markdown block in the entire virtualized root. Since the virtualizer can render overscan rows outside the viewport, an offscreen `[data-markdown-key="initial"]` can delay `firstPaint` (and the test’s wait) even though `firstPaintNodes` only tracks viewport-visible rows. Consider limiting the check to `initial` blocks that intersect the viewport so the probe only waits for hydration of content that can affect the `removed` count.

This block adds stdio error listeners unconditionally, but `packages/cli/src/node/index.ts` already attaches an `error` listener to `process.stdout` before importing this module. Importing via the Node wrapper will therefore register duplicate listeners. Also, `"code" in error` can throw if the emitted value isn’t an object (e.g. `null`/primitive), which would reintroduce an unhandled exception during logging.

Consider making the guard idempotent (so it’s safe when `index.ts` is imported by multiple entrypoints) and hardening the `EPIPE` check to avoid `in` on non-objects.

In the dev-server path, `version` is hard-coded to "local", but `Service.ensure` does a strict equality check against the running service’s `/api/health` version. When the Desktop dev script sets `OPENCODE_VERSION` (e.g. `2.0.0-local-<timestamp>`), this will never match and `Service.ensure` will continuously treat the service as incompatible and restart/never become ready.

This does not use `process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION`. In `packages/cli/src/version.ts`, `OPENCODE_VERSION` is a declared compile-time global and source execution falls back to `"local"`. The CLI passes that same imported value into `Runtime.run`, which supplies the server health version. I also verified the exact dev command with `OPENCODE_VERSION=2.0.0-local-...`; `bun run --cwd packages/cli dev -- --version` reports `opencode vlocal`. Therefore `Service.ensure` and `/api/health` both use `local` in this path.

`startServer` can race with itself (e.g., user triggers restart twice quickly): multiple in-flight `spawnSidecar` calls can resolve out of order, and the older one will still `sidecars.set(id, sidecar)` and mark the server `ready`, potentially leaving the newer sidecar untracked/running or overwriting state with stale credentials. The previous implementation’s attempt/generation tracking prevented this, but it’s been removed here.

`stopServer` no longer guards against exceptions from `existing.stop()`. If the child process already exited or a future `stop` implementation throws, this can crash the main process during shutdown/restart paths.

When `--single` selects no targets on an unsupported platform/arch, this throws `Unknown build target: undefined`, which is misleading (the target wasn’t explicitly requested). It also makes debugging flag combinations harder.

`--target=` with an empty value sets `requestedTarget` to "" (falsy), so the script falls back to building all targets instead of failing fast. This makes `--target=` behave unexpectedly and can trigger an expensive full build by mistake.

startServer has no guard against concurrent calls for the same id. If startServer is invoked twice (e.g. auto-start + user click, or repeated IPC calls), whichever spawn resolves last wins, and an older in-flight start can overwrite a newer one and/or leave an untracked sidecar running.

This issue also appears on line 196 of the same file.

Fixed in f9f7cd1c47. Target selection now checks `requestedTarget !== undefined`, so `--target=` selects no targets and fails with `Unknown build target` instead of falling back to the full build matrix. Verified with the build script directly.

Leaving this unchanged intentionally. The supported UI does not issue concurrent starts for one server: retry is unavailable while runtime is `starting`, and mutations are disabled while pending. Handling duplicated direct IPC calls would restore lifecycle bookkeeping that this refactor deliberately removes in favor of the normal user flow.

`toOaCompatibleRequest` can still emit function tools with a missing/undefined `function.name` if a tool has `type: "function"` but neither `tool.function?.name` nor top-level `tool.name` is present. That recreates the original upstream 400 (`tools[N].function: missing field "name"`). Also, if all tools are filtered out, sending `tools: []` is riskier than omitting `tools` entirely; omitting matches the existing behavior when no tools are provided.

Could we prevent the old run from publishing status after the replacement starts? Since `startRun` happens before the old fiber is interrupted, its interruption handler can publish `idle` after the replacement publishes `busy`, and CLI/TUI consumers may treat the active replacement as complete. Is this a concern?

Could we defer failing `old.done` until the old fiber has completed interruption cleanup? Failing it here wakes `onInterrupt` (`lastAssistant`) before interruption begins, so a synchronous prompt caller can receive an assistant message whose tool is still running and whose completion/error metadata is not finalized. Is this a concern?

Good point. I addressed this by making the replacement work wait until the old run has finished interruption cleanup. The interruption still runs on an independent fiber so `finishRun` can acquire the `SynchronizedRef` without deadlocking. In addition, `finishRun` keeps its run-ID guard, so a replaced run cannot publish `idle` for the active replacement. I added regression coverage that holds the old cleanup open and verifies that no stale `idle` is published while the replacement is active.

Yes, this was a real concern. I removed the eager failure of `old.done`; it is now completed by the old fiber through the existing `finishRun` path after interruption cleanup has finished. This prevents `onInterrupt` / `lastAssistant` from returning while the tool and its metadata are still being finalized. I also added regression coverage for this ordering, successive replacements, and cancellation while a replacement is waiting.

This table row has a large amount of trailing whitespace before the closing `|`, which creates diff noise and can trip whitespace/markdown linters. Trim the padding so the line ends cleanly like the other rows.
we can remove `from` here right, it defauts to project's dir

Yes. Made `from` optional and removed it here. Core now defaults to the project table’s primary `worktree` directory, then performs the same tracked-directory validation as an explicit `from`. The TUI still passes `from` explicitly when creating from the current managed worktree. Fixed in 659e6c75a1.

Calling `ctx.sync.session.sync(...)` directly inside this `createEffect` will track the reactive reads performed by `sync` (it reads `data.message[...]`, `meta.limit[...]`, etc.), which can cause this effect to re-run repeatedly as session data loads/updates. That re-run loop is unnecessary work and can undermine the navigation-performance goal. Consider deferring the call (or using `untrack`) so `sync` executes outside the reactive tracking scope.

The polling loop never checks `abort.signal.aborted`, so in `test` mode (where `readStatus` ignores the signal) the loop keeps running after `onCleanup()` aborts, leaking timers/network work during HMR/unmounts. Guard the loop with the abort signal so it always terminates promptly on cleanup.

`blobID` accesses the global `crypto` identifier directly. In environments where `crypto` is not defined (or where the API exists but is blocked in non-secure contexts), this will still throw before the fallback runs. Elsewhere in the app (`utils/uuid.ts`) the pattern is to use `globalThis.crypto` and guard `globalThis.isSecureContext`.

Consider switching to `globalThis.crypto?.subtle` (and optionally `isSecureContext`) so the fallback is guaranteed to run instead of raising a `ReferenceError` / security error.

`integration(providerID)` does a linear `.find()` over `integrations.list()` each time it’s called, and it’s invoked multiple times per row (via `source()` and `canDisconnect()`). This can become O(rows × integrations) and adds avoidable work during render; prefer indexing the list once (memoized) and doing O(1) lookups.

This issue also appears on line 105 of the same file.

buildPromptRequest concatenates formatted file-comment notes into the single user `text` field. Downstream, `normalizeSessionMessages.userParts` turns `message.text` into a non-synthetic `text` part, so the timeline’s `MessageComment.fromPart` (which only extracts comments from `part.synthetic` + `readCommentMetadata`/`parseCommentNote`) can no longer recognize file-comment notes as structured comments. If the UI still needs structured comment rendering, consider emitting comment notes as separate synthetic parts/messages (or splitting `message.text` into a normal text part plus synthetic comment-note parts with `opencodeComment` metadata derived from `parseCommentNote`).

For `session.moved`, `event.current.location.directory` represents the *source* directory (see `session.moved` schema + existing tests), while the destination directory is `event.current.data.location.directory`. Using `event.current.location.directory` here makes `previousDirectory` equal `directory`, so `markSessionListChanged` won’t bump the destination directory revision and in-flight session list loads for the destination can return stale data.

`createDirSdkContext` now attaches a `serverSDK.event.listen` handler per directory context and filters in userland. With multiple active DirectorySDK instances, every server event will run through N directory filters, which can become a hot path during high-volume streams (e.g., deltas). Consider dispatching by directory once in the base SDK (e.g., a single listener that routes into per-directory emitters / a refcounted map) so each event is classified once.

Valid. The event envelope location is the source and event.data.location is the destination. Commit 52d7b3d87c now derives and invalidates both locations, with a regression test. The stale destination revision was pre-existing because the old directory channel also used the source envelope location.

Valid. Commit 52d7b3d87c adds one internal real-location emitter in the base SDK, so each event is classified once. The public emitter remains keyed by event type like the TUI, and directory SDKs subscribe only to their real location.

On Windows this test assumes `dir.path` contains backslashes so that `directory.replaceAll("\\", "/")` produces a different string; if `dir.path` is already returned with `/` separators (possible depending on runtime/FS APIs), `alternate === directory` and the `win32` assertion will fail (and the cache-key expectation may mismatch the canonical `path.normalize` output). Consider constructing an alternate path that is guaranteed to differ on win32, and compute the expected cached key using the same normalization as production code.

extractPromptFromMessage derives the restored file attachment path from file.name when the mention text doesn’t start with "@". If the user mentioned a path like "src/client.ts" (no leading @), this will restore the attachment with a path like "client.ts", losing directory context and potentially breaking selection/restore.
